issues.description: Field Note.creationDate has conflicting types between the common model and the server service. In the template repository, src/common/java/de/tum/in/ase/eist/model/Note.java declares creationDate as java.time.Instant. The server code (both template and solution) in src/server/java/de/tum/in/ase/eist/service/NoteService.java calls note.setCreationDate(Instant.now()), i.e. expects an Instant. However the solution repository's shared model at src/common/java/de/tum/in/ase/eist/model/Note.java declares creationDate as String. This mismatch (Instant vs String) will cause compilation errors (setCreationDate(Instant) does not exist on a Note with String field) and will confuse students when comparing the template, the provided solution, and the problem statement example which shows an ISO-8601 instant value for creationDate.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the Note.creationDate type consistent across all artifacts. Preferred fix: change the solution repository's common Note model to declare creationDate as java.time.Instant (with matching getter/setter accepting Instant) so it matches NoteService and the template model. Alternatively, if a String is desired in the shared model, update the server NoteService to set a formatted ISO-8601 String (e.g. Instant.now().toString()) and adjust all call sites and the problem statement examples accordingly. Ensure template, solution, and server/service code use the same type to avoid compilation errors.
